proposal.name: Stream gate recordings through owned temporary files

plan.name: Stream gate recordings through owned temporary files
plan.summary: Connect the complete step #569 of parent #549 in one pull request: verify.Run, including the factory's in-process gate, uses owned file-backed recordings and conformance.CheckReader for Go Try, ordinary Python and TypeScript, existing TypeScript, and sampled or explored existing Python applications, while Language.Check and Evidence.Traces keep their byte-returning compatibility contracts and Go without Try keeps agreement alone. Retain recordings until consumption, then close and remove all owned recording and conversion storage on success, semantic failure, unrelated gate errors and cancellation; preserve driver commands, mounts, environment, seeds, sandbox markers, diagnostics and the distinction between absent, empty and malformed evidence, without buffering recordings or retaining descriptors per queued batch. Convert authenticated Python observations incrementally with disk-backed state deduplication, preserving first-seen identities, module-value conversion, exact integers, replay filtering, declared outcomes, raw ordered receipt evidence, hashes, invocation identity, provenance and JSON-round-trip fingerprints, with no second recording-sized tree or JSON buffer for conformance. Validate end-to-end gate counts, verdicts, lifetime and cleanup with command-boundary stand-ins and isolated peak-heap measurements at fixed batch size and concurrency, preserve existing compatibility, authority, failure and fingerprint suites unchanged, run affected Go tests and the affected real Python and TLAPS opt-ins in PR CI, and leave unavailable Docker/network checks to Merger work. Update SPEC.md and docs/gate.md with this plan, recorded conformance and Python foundations, the part-1 bounded-storage policy, accurately measured workload ceilings, growing compact indexes and proportional temporary disk, and the separate costs of TLC containers, drivers and retained receipt evidence; the merger records the evidence-ownership decision and any still-unrecorded part-1 storage decision, without the build writing decisions/.

tests.name: TestGateRecordingPeakHeap
tests.says: Real verify.Run production, handoff, decoding and conformance checking stay below one 192 MiB peak-heap ceiling when file-backed recordings double from 32,768 to 65,536 distinct 8 KiB states, for Go Try and ordinary TypeScript, with exact successful and late-failure counts and verdicts.

tests.name: TestGateRefusedRecordingPeakHeap
tests.says: Many distinct refused attempts over one state use bounded transport memory through verify.Run and retain exact attempt counts and successful coverage, at both recording sizes.

tests.name: TestGateRecordingOwnershipAndCompatibility
tests.says: All built-in file producers keep their recording available through conformance, clean up after success, failures and cancellation, retain direct byte evidence, preserve absent versus invalid recordings and diagnostics, and leave Go without Try agreement-only.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationRecordingTransport
tests.says: Sampled and explored authenticated Python applications run through the gate's owned streaming transport, retaining ordered raw evidence, exact numbers, module conversion, replay and strict-refusal semantics, provenance and round-trip fingerprints.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationConversionPeakHeap
tests.says: Incremental sampled and explored conversion writes the same semantic recording without a second recording-sized tree or buffer; doubling large observations keeps additional conversion heap bounded, with cancellation and write errors propagated.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and five acceptance tests covering streaming ownership, bounded memory, cleanup, compatibility, and Python receipt preservation in one complete change. The plan checker passed on the first check; all five tests fail on the baseline as required, and `repo/` remains unchanged.
